submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the head noun ' government' (space-prefixed; ' Government' about half as strong) when it names the national/central state as an acting party, e.g. 'the (federal) government', strongest (5-10) as a party in legal or policy dispute clauses like 'argues that the government ...', and weaker (1.5-3.5) on other national state-authority nouns used the same way (' administration', ' Congress', ' agency', ' authorities', ' CIA', ' State', ' officials', ' court' after 'trial'). It is near zero on every other token (no floor), on 'local government', ' governor', private parties (company, contractor, neighbors, police), the bare modifier ' federal', and the employer sense 'works for the government'.
